items.name: OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra
items.summary: OpenAI's fast everyday-work model, launched October 26, combines visual reasoning with precise computer use and clearer writing at 50% lower standard API prices than GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol. It is available in ChatGPT Work and Codex and via the API as gpt-6.1-terra, and OpenAI says it finishes tasks over 3x faster than GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol.

items.name: Moonshot AI Kimi K3.1 Pro
items.summary: Moonshot's post-trained Kimi K3, released October 23, keeps 2.8 trillion total parameters (104 billion active) and a 1M-token context, scoring 55 on Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index — fourth overall and the highest open-weight score recorded there. It costs $2/$10 per million tokens, with full open weights promised by November 4, 2026.

items.name: MiniMax M3.1 Flash (open weights)
items.summary: MiniMax published the weights for M3.1 Flash on October 23, four days after its API launch: a 428-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 23 billion active per token, a 1M-token context, and text, image and video input. It is built for coding, agents and computer-use tasks, with deployment support for vLLM and SGLang.

items.name: Recursive Flint
items.summary: Recursive's first model, released October 21 under Apache 2.0, is a 39.8-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts coder with only about 2.5 billion active parameters per token, designed to run coding agents locally on a laptop. Recursive reports over 125 tokens per second on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro with its optimised engine, keeping source code on-device.

items.name: Mistral Voxtral 3
items.summary: Mistral's Voxtral 3 family, released October 20, bundles speech-to-text and text-to-speech models with a LiveKit-based voice-agent SDK into one streaming pipeline for real-time voice agents. Transcription covers over 50 languages and text-to-speech over 35 languages, with agents able to call external systems mid-conversation.
